prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, in which heterobifunctional molecules bring a chosen protein and a ubiquitin ligase together so that the protein is removed

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B007 to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Five of eight members now carry B007 in their preferred configuration, but I do not rely on the count. The scientific case is that a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase, that the cooperativity of this complex is a measurable, tunable physical quantity, and that ubiquitination and proteasomal removal follow. It is a mechanism stated in physical terms and tested by binding and kinetic experiments, which is what I weigh most. The principle has been confirmed independently by many academic and industrial groups and across several ligases, so the scientific basis does not wait for a drug approval. On credit, Crews and Deshaies introduced the concept in 2001, and Ciulli's VHL ligand chemistry and structural account of cooperativity turned it into a rational design discipline. This slate is the one that four members (Aqvist, Chabes in part, Linke and I) converge on, and Aili has said he would accept Deshaies over Handa. I withdraw B044 as a candidate for this year: it drew no support and I could not answer Sparr's doubt that it adds beyond Marcus theory.
statement.case_against: The residual weaknesses are real. First, PROTACs and cereblon molecular glues are partly separate strands, and a three-name prize leaves out Handa, Ito, Gray and Sakamoto, whose claims a careful reader will see; the citation must be worded so that it does not read as a judgment that the glue branch is unimportant, yet I do not think the committee can credit it honestly within three names. Second, no degrader is an approved drug as far as I can verify, so the medical payoff is still prospective, and the 2001 paper was a proof of concept with peptidic molecules, so the line between founding discovery and later drug-like refinement must be argued carefully. Third, if the expert reports show that the clinical status of the late-stage programmes is weaker than assumed, or that Ciulli's contribution is better seen as refinement than as essential, I would turn to B052 or B029.

responses.point: Aili keeps Handa in the third seat to cover the cereblon glue branch but says he would accept Deshaies over Handa if the committee prefers a pure PROTAC citation, and asks for priority and not influence as the argument.
responses.response: I read this as the main open question for B007, and my answer rests on priority. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which is a mechanism-of-action discovery about an existing drug, while the design principle that lets a chemist build a degrader for a chosen target was published by Crews and Deshaies in 2001. I therefore keep Deshaies, and I welcome your willingness to accept him. I do not want the glue strand treated as lesser, so I would keep the citation to induced-proximity degradation, in wording that leaves the cereblon work open for a later and separately argued recognition instead of dropping it silently.

responses.point: Chabes anchors B007 on Crews and Deshaies as a two-person part beside Liu for B052, drops Ciulli and Handa under the three-person cap, and argues that glue degraders should be a separate later part.
responses.response: We agree on the glue question and on Deshaies. Where I differ is the two-part prize. I find your argument against blurring two stories persuasive, but I think a single coherent achievement is the stronger public statement, and the Ciulli seat is not decoration: the quantitative cooperativity and VHL structural work is the part of the field I can judge as a physical mechanism, and without it the 2001 concept stays a peptide proof of concept. I would also ask whether base editing is distinct enough from the 2020 prize to carry a part. I think it can be argued, but it needs a citation about a deamination reaction on DNA and I would not make it a condition of awarding B007.

responses.point: Linke asks, in his reply to Aqvist, whether a later year after an approval would be a better moment, since that is the real cost of acting now, and keeps B001 as an alternative.
responses.response: I accept the question as the right test. My answer is that this citation is for a chemical principle, ternary-complex formation and its cooperativity, and that principle is independently confirmed whether or not any degrader is approved; waiting would add clinical proof but would not change the science. The cost of waiting is also not zero, since the priority set is ageing and the attribution problem does not get easier. I still want the expert report to state the status of the late-stage trials, and if it contradicts the assumption of broad clinical progress I will weigh that. On B001 I remain where you are: the physical framework is elegant, but the in vivo status is unresolved and I could not name three people with confidence.

responses.point: Zou pairs B029 with Liu's B052 as two mature, well-attributed achievements, and regards B007 as a real alternative that is more crowded and less settled.
responses.response: I understand preferring cases with two clear originators, and I share your view that Buchwald and Hartwig and Liu are cleaner attributions than the degrader slate. My difficulty with the pairing is that it is two prizes with no shared theme, and B029 still has to show it is a conceptual step beyond the 2010 prize, which I asked Somfai about and which I did not see answered in your statement. I would take B029 as a real fallback, but I do not find B007 less settled on the science: the ternary-complex principle is quantitatively established, and what remains open is attribution and clinical timing.

responses.point: Somfai argues that C-N coupling is mature, overdue and that amine binding, deprotonation and beta-hydride avoidance make it distinct from the 2010 prize, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the clean pair and Kosugi as a precursor.
responses.response: Your point on amine binding and beta-hydride avoidance moves me a little, since it identifies a mechanistic problem that the 2010 chemistry did not have to solve, and I now put B029 as my second alternative. I still read it as an outstanding extension within an already recognised catalytic framework, whereas degradation introduces a different mechanism of action. I also agree with you and Zou that Kosugi is a precursor and not a co-originator, so I withdraw the three-name version I proposed in my opening.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat PROTACs and cereblon molecular glues as one achievement or two, which would decide whether Handa and Ito belong in the citation.
The current clinical status of degraders in late-stage trials, which I have not verified and which bears on how firmly maturity can be asserted.
Whether Ciulli's contribution is judged essential or a refinement of the 2001 concept, which determines the third seat if the report is critical.
Whether the committee will accept C-N coupling (B029) as a conceptual step beyond the 2010 prize, since that decides the strength of my fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any B007 candidate or other shortlisted name is apparent from my profile, and I report no recusal. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not a conflict with any candidate. My opening first choice, B044, touches electron-transfer research in my own field of respiratory enzymes; I have withdrawn it and do not include it in the preferred configuration or the alternatives.
